title: Explicit Absolutely Maximally Entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power
problem: An absolutely maximally entangled state AME\((N,d)\) has every reduction to half the parties maximally mixed. Tensoring AME\((N,m)\) with AME\((N,n)\) gives AME\((N,mn)\), but a local dimension \(2q\) would need an AME state of qubits, and those exist only for \(N=2,3,5,6\). Stabilizer constructions face the same obstruction. Which local dimensions admit AME states of nine and more parties, and can the missing factor of two be supplied another way?
result: A superposition \(\sum_a\sqrt{\lambda_a}\ket{u_a}\ket{v_a}\) is AME\((N,2q)\) if the qubit states' mixture has maximally mixed \(k\)-party reductions (\(k=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\)) and the \(q\)-level states come from projecting one party of an AME\((N+1,q)\) parent, which cancels every interference term. This gives explicit AME\((N,2q)\) for all odd prime powers \(q\ge5\) at \(N=9\) and 11, \(q\ge17\) at 13, \(q\ge9\) at 15 and \(q\ge67\) at 17, and for every odd \(N\) when \(q\ge\max\{N,2^{N-2}\}\). Combined with known states, AME\((9,d)\) exists if and only if \(d\ge3\). For \(q\ge N\) the coupling works exactly when some \(k\)-uniform \(N\)-qubit mixture has rank at most \(q\), and proved rank bounds show the \(N=15\) threshold cannot be lowered within this method.
significance: The nine-party existence question is now settled for every integer local dimension; the first new case is \(d=14\). The construction also separates two tasks, finding a low-rank uniform qubit mixture and finding a parent, so progress on either transfers directly.
limitations: The thresholds are sufficient, not necessary: within the coupling, \(q=9,11,13\) at \(N=13\) and \(23\le q\le61\) at \(N=17\) remain open, and other ways of cancelling interference could reach smaller dimensions, possibly AME\((13,10)\). The nine-party classification depends on Kitamura's external AME\((9,6)\) state, which this coupling cannot produce. Finite inputs (qubit groups, small-field parents) are certified by exact computation in a companion repository rather than in the text. The paper builds on a nine-qubit mixture from the AME\((9,10)\) state of the Atlas Lean library and on Kitamura's eleven-party construction; it contains no AI-use statement.
summary_basis: Description based on the full arXiv HTML of v1, read 2026-11-14: Sections I–III and Appendices B.1–B.2 (the qubit groups) and G.2 (the mixture for every odd \(N\)); Appendices A, C–F and G.1, G.3 were not read beyond what the main text cites. The weight enumerator of the fifteen-qubit group was recomputed, and the coupling was checked on a small explicit instance.

methods_basis: Based on the linked paper version. Derivations marked as editorial, and suggested uses in other problems, are editorial guidance rather than results of the paper.
description: For \(N=2k+1\) parties of local dimension \(d\), AME\((N,d)\) means \(\rho_A=\mathbb I/d^k\) for every set \(A\) of \(k\) parties. The product rule makes composite dimensions easy once their factors are available, so dimensions \(d=2s\) with \(s\) odd are the hard case: no AME state of nine or more qubits exists. Moreover, for odd \(q\) a stabilizer AME\((N,2q)\) state in the cyclic Weyl convention would yield a stabilizer qubit AME state, so the new states cannot be stabilizer states in that convention.

The coupling identifies a qubit and a \(q\)-level system at each site with one \(2q\)-level system, \(\ket b\ket j\leftrightarrow\ket{qb+j}\), and sets \[\ket\Psi=\sum_{a=0}^{K-1}\sqrt{\lambda_a}\,\ket{u_a}\otimes\ket{v_a}.\] Reducing to \(A\) produces terms \(\mathrm{Tr}_{A^c}\ket{u_a}\bra{u_b}\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{A^c}\ket{v_a}\bra{v_b}\). If the \(q\)-level cross blocks vanish for \(a\ne b\) and equal \(\mathbb I/q^k\) for \(a=b\), only the average \(\sum_a\lambda_a\mathrm{Tr}_{A^c}\ket{u_a}\bra{u_a}\) survives on the qubit side. That average can be maximally mixed even though no single qubit state is.

Qubit mixtures come from commuting Pauli groups: the normalised projector \(P/K\) onto the joint fixed space is \(k\)-uniform exactly when every nonidentity group element acts on more than \(k\) qubits. For \(N=15\) a cyclic code over \(\mathbb F_4\) gives 12 generators, rank \(K=8\) and minimum weight 8. Shortening gives \(N=13\) (\(K=16\), weight 7), and a quasicyclic \([18,6,10]_4\) code gives \(N=17\) (\(K=64\), weight 9). For any odd \(N\), the group generated by \(X^{\otimes2k}\otimes I\) and \(Z^{\otimes2k}\otimes I\) works with \(K=2^{N-2}\). At \(N=9,11\) the known Atlas and Kitamura mixtures have 4 and 2 branches.

Parents are Cauchy-matrix MDS graph states, which exist for prime powers \(q\ge N+1\), and in extended form for \(q=N\) when \(N\) is a prime power; special parents cover \(q=5\) at \(N=9,11\) and \(q=9\) at \(N=15\). A parent supplies at most \(q\) branches, so \(q\ge K\) is also needed, which fixes the thresholds. For nine parties, odd \(d\) and multiples of 4 follow from prime-power constructions. For \(d=2s\) with \(s\) odd, use AME\((9,6)\) when \(3\mid s\) and otherwise AME\((9,2p)\) for a prime \(p\ge5\) dividing \(s\), times an odd factor. Rains' shadow bound excludes \(d=2\).

Limits of the coupling: no more than \(q\) branches can have vanishing cross blocks, and a \(k\)-uniform mixture of \(N\) qubits has rank at least 4, 9, 8 and 23 for \(N=9,13,15,17\), with the required dimension growing at least exponentially in \(N\). Choosing which qubit branch pairs with which parent branch also lets the construction impose symmetry: for primes \(p\equiv1\pmod{15}\), starting at 31, there is an AME\((15,2p)\) state with a cyclic shift of all parties compensated by local unitaries. A concrete open target is a six-uniform 13-qubit mixture of rank 9 to 13, which would give AME\((13,26)\).

methods.technique: Erasing interference with a parent's projected branches
methods.explanation: The qubit side can only be made uniform on average, so the interference between branches must be removed completely on every \(k\)-party cut. Projecting the extra party of an AME state with one more party gives states whose reduced cross terms vanish, because that party counts towards the cut.
math: Editorial derivation of the projection step. Let \(\ket\Phi\) be AME\((N+1,q)\) with reference party \(R\), and \(\ket{v_a}=\sqrt q\,(\mathbb I\otimes\bra a_R)\ket\Phi\). For a set \(A\) of \(k=(N-1)/2\) parties, \(A\cup R\) has \(k+1=(N+1)/2\) parties, half of \(N+1\), so \(\rho_{AR}=\mathbb I/q^{k+1}\). Hence \[\mathrm{Tr}_{A^c}\ket{v_a}\bra{v_b}=q\,\langle a\vert_R\,\rho_{AR}\,\vert b\rangle_R=\delta_{ab}\,\frac{\mathbb I_A}{q^k},\] and the reduction of \(\ket\Psi\) is \((\sum_a\lambda_a\mathrm{Tr}_{A^c}\ket{u_a}\bra{u_a})\otimes\mathbb I/q^k=\mathbb I/(2q)^k\).

Editorial check on the smallest case, \(N=3\), \(q=3\): branches \(\ket{u_b}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}(\ket{00}+\ket{11})\ket b\) for \(b=0,1\), and the parent \(\tfrac13\sum_{i,j}\ket{i,j,i+j,i+2j}\), which is AME\((4,3)\). The coupled state in \((\mathbb C^6)^{\otimes3}\) has every single-party reduction equal to \(\mathbb I/6\) to machine precision, while a single branch \(\ket{u_0}\) has a reduction that differs from \(\mathbb I/2\) by 0.5 in one entry. AME\((3,6)\) is known anyway (a GHZ state); the example only exhibits the mechanism.
methods.transfer: When a product construction needs a factor that does not exist, ask whether only its average is needed. A second factor whose states have vanishing reduced cross terms, such as branches projected from a larger code or AME state, can convert an average condition into a pure-state one.

methods.technique: The weight test for uniform stabilizer mixtures
methods.explanation: The qubit ingredient must be a mixed state of low rank with maximally mixed \(k\)-party reductions. Pauli groups make both properties checkable from a weight enumerator: the rank is \(2^{N-r}\) and uniformity is a minimum-weight condition.
math: For an abelian group \(S\) of Hermitian Pauli words with \(r\) independent generators and \(-\mathbb I\notin S\), \[\frac{P}{K}=2^{-N}\sum_{E\in S}E,\qquad K=2^{N-r}.\] Tracing out any qubit on which a word acts nontrivially kills that word, so \(\mathrm{Tr}_{A^c}(P/K)\) keeps only words supported inside \(A\). Distinct Pauli words are linearly independent, so the reduction is \(\mathbb I/2^k\) for every \(k\)-set exactly when no nonidentity word has weight at most \(k\).

Editorial check of Proposition B.1 at \(N=15\): the word \(XYXIXYIZZXIIIII\), its cyclic shifts by \(0,\dots,5\) and their images under \(X\to Z\to Y\to X\) give 12 pairwise commuting generators of rank 12 over \(\mathbb F_2\). The 4096 group elements have weights 0, 8, 10, 12 and 14 with multiplicities 1, 405, 1260, 1890 and 540, as stated; the minimum weight 8 exceeds 7, so \(P/8\) is 7-uniform. With the rank bound of 8 at \(N=15\), the threshold \(q\ge9\) is optimal for this coupling.
methods.transfer: To find low-rank mixed states with uniform marginals, search additive codes over \(\mathbb F_4\) for large minimum weight rather than large distance: the fixed-space projector needs only heavy stabilizer elements, a weaker condition than for a pure AME state.
